key_concepts: Living things breathe, eat, grow, move, and reproduce.
Non-living things do not need to eat to remain.
Living things depend on other things, especially non-living things, to survive.
Non-living things can remain in the world without depending on other things.
Plants and trees are living things rooted in soil or water.
Soil and water are non-living things that provide nutrients for plants.
Plants need sunlight and carbon dioxide from the air to live.
Carbon dioxide in the air comes partly from the breathing of animals and humans.
Plants reproduce through seeds, leaves, branches, and roots.
Living and non-living things are connected to each other.
Every living or non-living thing has an important role in the environment.
People, animals, plants, fish, insects, and mushrooms are examples of living things.
